office: the Civil and Identity Registry (National Identity Office)

routes.label: registration with the NID office, with the birth certificate
a stolen, damaged or lost NID card replaced

note: EMTV, quoting the registry: the NID card comes with the new birth certificate for those 18 and older, the age the Civil Registration Act sets for holding it; The National: the card is free, the minister responsible says, and no one is to pay. Its term and the time aren't stated. The Civil and Identity Registry's own pages (read 2026-11-03): the NID card section of its registration form is for applicants of 18 and above, and its statutory fee table (from 1 January 2015) prices a replaced NID card (stolen, damaged, lost) at K200, held, and no first card, which agrees with the minister's word that the first card is free; the table doesn't say so in words, so the entry stays at second hand.

sources.title: EMTV (Papua New Guinea), on the new birth certificate and NID card
sources.said: He explained that the new birth certificate comes along with a NID card for those at 18 years of age and older.

sources.title: EMTV (Papua New Guinea), on the NID component of the Civil Registration Act
sources.said: the NID component is an extension of the Civil Registration Act that calls for a person to have a National Identification Card by 18 years of Age.

sources.title: The National (Papua New Guinea), No fee for NID card, says Maru
sources.said: THE National Identification Card (NID) is free and anyone charging for it to be processed should be reported to police
